title: Circuit-balance harmonics and SLO realignment after staggered region evacuation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-16 we observed an SLO miss across two regions triggered during a planned staggered evacuation of primary-region capacity. Root cause analysis showed a correlated oscillation between per-region circuit-breaker damping parameters and token-bucket refill skew. The evacuation sequence caused one region to enter a conservative shed mode while the other region ramped up traffic; combined with mismatched hysteresis timers and KV-cache rewarm delays, this produced sustained tail-latency spikes and an elevated 99th percentile token latency that crossed our SLO threshold for ~27 minutes. This ticket captures the investigation timeline, engineering findings, decisions, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

analysis: Primary vector: sequencing mismatch. During staged evacuation we express-migrated traffic; the control plane's TTL for circuit hysteresis was asymmetric between regions because of an older rollout variant in region B (legacy config).

Amplifier: token-bucket refill skew. Region A's token buckets refilled with a 1s skew relative to region B due to clock drift on the autoscaler agent; under surge this produced microbursts that pushed region B into frequent CB transitions.
KV cache factor: cold prefixes in region B increased backend compute time by ~22% for affected requests; cache warmup is slower for large sequence inputs because of batch size limits during failover.
Fallback orchestration: the routing policy used a 'first healthy' affinity that favored region B after partial drain of A, worsening the load imbalance instead of smoothing it.
Observability gaps: no per-token-latency trendline tied to circuit-state was present in the default SLO dashboard; correlate CB state with token latency required ad-hoc queries.
decisions: Immediate: patch rollout to align circuit hysteresis defaults across regions and reject region-level config drift at control plane admission. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4789
Short-term: implement a per-region smoothing window on routing decisions (token-bucket smoothing) with a 5s sliding median to prevent microburst fanout.
Medium-term: unify circuit-breaker config behind a single source-of-truth and introduce a canary gating step for CB parameter rollouts.
Long-term: add a region-aware KV cache pre-warming phase when failover is anticipated by control plane, and simulate cold-warm transitions in chaos tests.
